security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are Markdown fences, slash-command examples, or JavaScript template literals and are false positives. Real risk remains where the skill instructs agents to run npx claude-flow@alpha, install command bundles globally, and write shell completion files under the home directory. No evidence found for prompt injection or data exfiltration intent.

remediation.suggestion: Pin claude-flow to a reviewed version or require users to verify the package before running any npx command.

remediation.issue: Global install and home directory writes
remediation.suggestion: Make global installation optional, document exact files changed, and require explicit confirmation before writing under the home directory.
Separate illustrative examples from commands intended for execution and require confirmation before running each shell block.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Alpha CLI Execution and Global Installation
semantic_findings.description: The workflow repeatedly asks users or agents to run npx claude-flow@alpha and install generated command bundles globally. This creates supply-chain and persistence risk because the alpha package is not pinned to an immutable version.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent slash commands that route micro-skills without confusing syntax. This skill guides command design, validation, handler generation, testing, documentation, and deployment steps.
actual_capabilities: Defines slash command names, aliases, parameters, flags, and examples.
Shows how to generate command schemas and handler templates.
Adds parameter validation, routing logic, and error handling patterns.
Defines test steps for registration, validation, errors, and integration behavior.
Creates documentation, help text, command catalogs, and usage examples.
Covers build, install, registry, and shell completion deployment steps.
limitations: The examples depend on Claude Flow commands and may need adaptation.
The skill does not audit generated command code for production security.
Global installation and shell completion steps require manual review.
It provides workflow guidance, not a complete command framework.

use_cases.title: Standardize Project Commands
use_cases.description: Create repeatable slash command patterns for code analysis, testing, and documentation tasks.

use_cases.title: Generate Command Handlers
use_cases.description: Plan handler structure, validation rules, routing targets, and error behavior before implementation.

use_cases.title: Prepare Command Documentation
use_cases.description: Produce command help text, usage examples, and command catalogs for team adoption.

prompt_templates.title: Define a Basic Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a slash command for [task]. Include the command name, required parameters, optional flags, and two examples.

prompt_templates.title: Add Validation Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create validation rules for [command]. Check required inputs, allowed ranges, default values, and helpful error messages.

prompt_templates.title: Generate and Test a Handler
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a handler for [command]. Include routing, parameter validation, test cases, and expected failure cases.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Command Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a slash command suite for [workflow]. Include command chaining, registry updates, documentation, deployment steps, and review gates.

output_examples.input: Create a slash command for code analysis.
output_examples.output: A command specification with name, alias, parameters, validation rules, examples, handler responsibilities, and test coverage.
A usage page that explains syntax, parameters, examples, output expectations, and related commands.
A deployment checklist covering build steps, installation validation, registry updates, completion generation, and rollback checks.

best_practices: Confirm every shell command before running it in a real project.
Keep command names short, specific, and consistent with existing workflows.
Validate required inputs and document failure messages before deployment.
anti_patterns: Installing generated commands globally before reviewing their contents.
Using broad command names that hide what the command does.
Skipping tests for required parameters, invalid paths, and expected errors.

faq.question: Does this skill create commands automatically?
faq.answer: It provides workflow steps and templates. Actual command generation still depends on the local Claude Flow tooling.

faq.question: Can it work with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata supports Codex, Claude, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it require Claude Flow?
faq.answer: The examples use Claude Flow commands. Replace them if your project uses another command framework.

faq.question: Is it safe to run every script directly?
faq.answer: No. Review npx commands, global installation, and home directory writes before execution.

faq.question: What commands does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on slash commands for micro-skill routing, validation, testing, documentation, and registry workflows.

faq.question: Can I adapt the templates?
faq.answer: Yes. Change command names, parameters, routing targets, tests, and documentation to fit your project.
